title: Request Slice Inspector with Correlation Tabs
creator: Sophie Lee
description: Design an embeddable Request Slice Inspector that sits as a right-side panel in the Redwood Console request detail page. The inspector surfaces a compact timeline, span swimlane, and a tabbed correlation pane that lets engineers quickly pivot between: Correlated Spans, KV / Cache Snapshots, Inference Payloads, and Cost Breakdown for that request. Goal is to reduce time-to-root-cause for production latency/cost regressions by making correlated context discoverable without leaving the request view.
goal: Make correlation-first debugging approachable: allow engineers to fluidly move from a single token latency spike on the timeline to the exact span, its sibling requests, relevant KV cache hits/misses, and incremental cost attribution, all within one compact inspector.
constraints: Must work at scale for requests with 500+ spans; keep initial render under 200ms for 95th percentile console loads; reuse existing span tile components where possible; maintain keyboard accessibility; support both Hosted and Dedicated request schemas (some fields are omitted in Dedicated logs).
proposed_solution: Right-side slide-over panel named 'Request Slice Inspector'. Top section: compact timeline canvas with scrubber and event markers (batching, cache hit/miss, fallback). Middle: virtualized span swimlane using existing SpanTile components with sibling-group collapse and quick-jump. Bottom: tabbed correlation pane with four tabs: Spans (linked view), KV Snapshot, Payload Preview (trimmed JSON + schema inference), Cost Breakdown (token-level attribution + model variant). Tabs load lazily; prefetch KV on mouseenter. Provide 'Open in Trace Studio' deep link to full trace page.
decisions: Use HTML/CSS list + canvas hybrid: canvas for timeline drawing (batch markers, scrubber) and virtualized divs for span tiles for easier accessibility and copy interactions.
Reuse SpanTile component and extend with a lightweight timeline indicator bar to show per-span latency distribution.
Tabbed correlation pane should be indexed by correlation-id and support 'show related requests' which triggers a lightweight query to the tracing API rather than full navigation.
Prefetch strategy: prefetch KV and cost metadata on panel hover (mouse enter) to keep initial open fast, cancel prefetch on mouseleave.
Accessibility: ensure the scrubber is keyboard-focusable and supports left/right arrow scrubbing by 100ms steps.
Performance: virtualize spans; cap DOM nodes to 80 visible span tiles and show 'n more' placeholder when collapsed.
Security: redact PII from payload preview by default; add toggle to reveal only for users with audit/view_payload privilege.
Scope: MVP will not include write-backs (editing KV) — view-only for now.
acceptance_criteria: Inspector opens as a slide-over from request detail and displays timeline + first 80 spans within 200ms on a cold load in staging console.
Tabs switch without full page navigation; KV tab shows the last known cache state associated with the request correlation-id.
Clicking a span focuses the timeline scrubber and highlights the KV & Payload entries that overlap that span's time window.
Cost tab displays token-level attribution for the selected span or request; numbers match backend cost-reporting dashboard within 5%.
Keyboard accessibility works for timeline scrubber, span list navigation (J/K or arrow keys), and tab switching (Ctrl+Tab).
No regressions in console render time for other pages; telemetry included to measure panel open time and tab load latencies.
Design review completed and prototype validated in at least two 45-minute usability sessions with platform and customer-facing engineers.
tasks: Finalize high-fidelity prototypes (Figma) for panel open/close states and collapsed span groups.
Prototype timeline canvas interactions (scrub, marker hover) in CodeSandbox to validate performance.
Spec API contract for traces/kv/cost endpoints with Eng (list of required fields and pagination strategy).
Implement accessibility checklist and keyboard mappings.
Coordinate with Privacy/Security to define payload redaction toggle and permission requirements.
Ship small feature flagged rollout to internal sandboxes for dogfooding.
Collect telemetry and refine thresholds before wider rollout.

Do we need a 'follow' mode that pins inspector changes to a single correlation-id when navigating related requests?
